why.title: Why {name}
why.sub: Each promise starts with why it matters. Open any of them for the whole story.
confidential.name: Confidential
confidential.why: What you most need help with is often what you’d rather keep to yourself: a payslip, a medical letter, a contract.
confidential.title: Kept on your device. On a capable computer, answered there too.
confidential.most: On the company’s servers, under its terms.
confidential.ours: On your device, encrypted. No {name} server.
confidential.offline: Turn off Wi-Fi and it still answers, on a computer with 12 GB of memory.
ai.name: Your AI
ai.why: AI changes every month, and you may already pay for one.
ai.title: Use the AI you want. Change it any time.
ai.ways: Your ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot plan
family.name: Ready for a family
family.why: Over half of US teens use AI for help with schoolwork, yet only about half of parents say their teen uses it at all.
family.title: A {name} for each child, set by you.
simple.name: Simple
simple.why: Most AI apps make you learn them first.
simple.title: One box. The rest when you need it.
simple.more: Day one: a question and a box. Nothing to learn first.
When it helps: an offer, in one sentence above the box, at the moment it’s useful. “No thanks” is for good.
Later: a game for the curious, each find saying how to find the next.
share.name: Shareable
share.why: A shared conversation is usually a copy the company can read.
share.title: Share it. Only they can read it.
share.limits: A password if you like · 30 days or a year
share.more: Sealed in your browser. Its key travels in the link, never to the host.
It opens as {name} drew it: charts, scores that play, pages that work.
Opened in someone’s {name}, it becomes their task, to carry on.
Or save it as one web page that opens in any browser.
open.name: Open
open.why: Apps change their rules, or close.
open.title: Open, all the way.
open.text: MIT, about 28,000 lines. Open standards, any AI, plain files.
catch.name: The catch
catch.title: The catch, plainly.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be.
No sign-up only with the AI on this computer.
catch.rest: That AI needs a recent computer: 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip. Not phones.
It can be wrong. Numbers are calculated; check the words, as you would a colleague’s.
Your work lives in this browser. Clear the browser’s data and it’s gone, unless you made a backup.
faq.title: Questions people ask
faq.items: Can I use it without signing up?
With the AI on this computer, yes. {free} asks for a free OpenRouter account.
Does it work with Excel and PDF files?
Yes, and with Word, PowerPoint, photos and whole folders. It hands back finished files too: a chart, a table, a document in Word.
Does it work on a phone, or offline?
On a phone, yes, in the browser. Offline, with the AI on this computer, which needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip: not on phones.
Can I use my ChatGPT or Claude plan?
Yes, and Copilot’s: {name} uses the plan you already pay for, through this computer. No second subscription.
Yes. Numbers are calculated rather than guessed, and under every answer it says where it was done. Check the words, as you would a colleague’s.
Can I use it at work?
If your company gives you nothing, it works as it is. If your computer is managed, ask your IT: {name} is deployed like a web page, behind your company’s gateway and sign-in.
